forbidden_inferences: catalytic inhibition from structural analogy to the alisertib warhead
catalytic inhibition from the rise in AURKA abundance
catalytic inhibition from a binary 'engaged' observation or from occupancy alone
absence of terminal effect from 'no significant' without an equivalence margin or detection limit
JB211 as a fully inactive or pharmacologically inert control
pT288_note: pT288 is a context-dependent activity proxy (cell-cycle dependent), not universal target engagement; occupancy, pT288, validated kinase activity, abundance and exposure are separate variables
t217d_note: T217D rescue is limited on-target evidence: wild-type overexpression also rescues, JB170 binding to T217D and HA-protein localisation are not reported, so it does not exclude degradation-specific effects, off-target effects or expression confounding

aurka_occupancy_or_binding.evidence: Results text says JB211 'binds AURORA-A but does not mediate its degradation'; no JB211 binding value found; BRET values are in Supp Table 1 (not_read); docking is a model

catalytic_activity.evidence: no pT288, substrate phosphorylation or kinase assay for JB211 in text or SI PDF

crbn_recruitment.evidence: by design (N-methylated glutarimide) and authors' statement; co-IP with JB211 exists in ED5c, result not read from the blot image

intracellular_exposure.evidence: no exposure, permeability or cellular concentration measurement

protein_abundance.evidence: IMR5, 1 uM, 6 h TMT (SI Supp Data Set 3): AURKA log2 reporter JB211 18.8811 +- 0.0309 (n=3), JB170 17.7434 (n=3), alisertib 19.3122 (n=4); one TMT batch, no vehicle channel; MV4-11 immunoblot: JB211 and alisertib raise AURKA (qualitative). Abundance only: it is not evidence of catalytic inhibition

terminal_phenotype.evidence: IMR5, 72 h, 0.5 and 1 uM: no significant apoptosis (Fig 6d) and no significant viability reduction (ED7d), n=3, two-tailed t-test; no equivalence margin, interval or detection limit

wording: CRBN-null close analog; AURKA binding is asserted in the source, but direct intracellular engagement and catalytic inhibition remain unresolved in the extracted evidence.
